title: VBench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
finding: Splits video generation quality into 16 disentangled dimensions (e.g. subject identity inconsistency, motion smoothness, temporal flickering, spatial relationship), each with tailored prompts and evaluators, and releases per-dimension human preference annotations to validate alignment with human perception.
why_for_us: Replace our single mean-frame-difference motion check with VBench's open, locally runnable dimension evaluators: subject consistency (speaker identity drift), temporal flickering, motion smoothness and dynamic degree, scored per clip on the 5090.

title: VBench++: Comprehensive and Versatile Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
finding: Extends VBench's 16 dimensions to image-to-video with a high-quality Image Suite with adaptive aspect ratio, adds trustworthiness evaluation, and open-sources prompts, generated videos and per-dimension human preference annotations.
why_for_us: Our shots are keyframe-conditioned, so the I2V part (consistency of the video with the conditioning image) is closer to our gate than plain T2V metrics; use it as a principled replacement or companion for the last-frame >=0.85 similarity rule.

title: VBench-2.0: Advancing Video Generation Benchmark Suite for Intrinsic Faithfulness
finding: Argues that per-frame aesthetics, temporal consistency and basic prompt adherence measure only superficial faithfulness; adds five intrinsic dimensions (Human Fidelity, Controllability, Creativity, Physics, Commonsense) evaluated with VLM/LLM generalists plus anomaly-detection specialists, validated by human annotation.
why_for_us: The Human Fidelity dimension (anatomy, face and hand correctness) targets exactly the talking-head failure modes our pixel metrics miss; worth adopting its human-anomaly checks as a separate gate signal.

title: EvalCrafter: Benchmarking and Evaluating Large Video Generation Models
finding: Evaluates T2V models on 700 prompts with 17 objective metrics covering visual, content, motion quality and text-video alignment, then fits coefficients to align the metrics with user opinions; per authors the fitted score correlates better with humans than a simple average of metrics.
why_for_us: Directly applicable recipe: once we have a few hundred human-reviewed clips, fit weights of our gate sub-metrics to the blind-review outcome instead of hand-set thresholds.

title: T2V-CompBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Compositional Text-to-video Generation
finding: First compositional T2V benchmark: 1400 prompts in seven categories (attribute binding, spatial relations, motion/action binding, object interactions, numeracy), scored with MLLM-, detection- and tracking-based metrics validated by correlation with human evaluation; current models find compositionality highly challenging.
why_for_us: Less central for talking heads, but its detection/tracking-based metrics are a template for checking prompt-specified actions (e.g. turns head, raises hand) in our keyframe shots.

title: Evaluation of Text-to-Video Generation Models: A Dynamics Perspective
finding: DEVIL protocol scores video dynamics at multiple temporal granularities (dynamics range, controllability, dynamics-based quality); per authors it reaches Pearson correlation above 90% with human ratings.
why_for_us: Our motion check is one mean frame difference in the upper 60% of frame; DEVIL shows motion should be graded against the intended dynamics level and at several time scales, which would catch both frozen heads and over-animated jitter.

title: VideoScore: Building Automatic Metrics to Simulate Fine-grained Human Feedback for Video Generation
finding: Learned video evaluator trained to simulate fine-grained, multi-aspect human feedback on generated videos (the OpenAlex record carries no abstract text, so no numbers are quoted here).
why_for_us: Open-weight video evaluator that can run locally next to ComfyUI; candidate per-aspect score to log for every clip and later correlate with our blind review; also the baseline VisionReward reports beating.

title: VideoScore2: Think before You Score in Generative Video Evaluation
finding: Multi-dimensional evaluator (visual quality, text alignment, physical/commonsense consistency) with chain-of-thought rationales, trained on 27,168 human-annotated videos via SFT then GRPO; per authors 44.35 (+5.94) accuracy in-domain and 50.37 (+4.32) average on four out-of-domain benchmarks, and useful for Best-of-N sampling.
why_for_us: Rationales make rejections explainable to reviewers; Best-of-N use matches rendering several seeds per shot and keeping one. Absolute accuracies (about 44-50) are modest, so use it to rank seeds, not as a hard pass/fail.

title: VisionReward: Fine-Grained Multi-Dimensional Human Preference Learning for Image and Video Generation
finding: Hierarchical, interpretable (linearly weighted) human-preference reward model for images and videos; per authors it surpasses VideoScore by 17.2% in preference prediction accuracy, and T2V models tuned with it reach a 31.6% higher pairwise win rate than with VideoScore.
why_for_us: Interpretable per-dimension checklist scores fit a gate better than one opaque number; strongest reported video preference gain among the open reward models found here, so a P0 candidate to benchmark on our own reviewed clips.

title: Improving Video Generation with Human Feedback
finding: Builds a large multi-dimensional pairwise human preference dataset for modern video generators and trains VideoReward, which per authors significantly outperforms existing video reward models; also introduces Flow-DPO, Flow-RWR and inference-time Flow-NRG for flow-based generators.
why_for_us: LTX is a flow-based model, so VideoReward is both a gate scorer and later a guidance or fine-tuning signal (Flow-NRG with custom weights for motion vs. visual quality).

title: ImageReward: Learning and Evaluating Human Preferences for Text-to-Image Generation
finding: First general-purpose text-to-image human preference reward model, trained on 137k expert comparisons; per authors it outperforms existing scoring models and metrics in human evaluation, and ReFL uses it to tune diffusion models.
why_for_us: Cheap per-keyframe scorer: run on conditioning keyframes before spending GPU minutes on video, and on sampled frames of finished clips as a sanity check.

title: Pick-a-Pic: An Open Dataset of User Preferences for Text-to-Image Generation
finding: Open dataset of real users' text-to-image preferences; the CLIP-based PickScore trained on it per authors shows superhuman performance at predicting preferences and correlates better with human rankings than other automatic metrics.
why_for_us: Shows the value of collecting our own reviewers' pairwise choices as training data; PickScore itself is a cheap local keyframe scorer.

title: Q-Align: Teaching LMMs for Visual Scoring via Discrete Text-Defined Levels
finding: Teaches LMMs to rate with discrete text-defined levels (as human raters do) instead of numeric scores, reaching state of the art on image quality, aesthetics and video quality assessment; OneAlign unifies the three tasks; weights released.
why_for_us: Open, locally runnable technical-quality scorer for blur, noise and compression; also a design hint for our review form: discrete labelled levels rather than free numeric scores.

title: AIGV-Assessor: Benchmarking and Evaluating the Perceptual Quality of Text-to-Video Generation with LMM
finding: AIGVQA-DB has 36,576 videos from 15 T2V models and 1,048 prompts with 370k expert ratings; AIGV-Assessor combines spatiotemporal features with an LMM to predict scores and pair preferences, per authors surpassing prior methods; generic VQA models fall short on AI-specific distortions.
why_for_us: Evidence that classic VQA models miss AI-specific artifacts (unnatural movement, inconsistent elements); its pairwise mode suits seed selection.

title: MLLM-as-a-Judge: Assessing Multimodal LLM-as-a-Judge with Vision-Language Benchmark
finding: Benchmarks MLLM judges on scoring, pair comparison and batch ranking; per authors MLLMs show human-like discernment in pair comparison but diverge significantly from humans in scoring and batch ranking, with biases, hallucinated responses and inconsistency even in GPT-4V.
why_for_us: If we add a VLM judge, ask it pairwise questions (clip A vs B, or clip vs reference keyframe) rather than absolute 1-10 scores, and never let it be the sole gate.

title: GenAI-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Compositional Text-to-Visual Generation
finding: Large human study of image and video generators on compositional prompts; VQAScore significantly outperforms CLIPScore, and ranking 3-9 candidates by VQAScore is per authors 2x-3x more effective than PickScore, HPSv2 or ImageReward; over 80,000 human ratings released.
why_for_us: VQAScore is an open, local way to check that a frame shows what the shot prompt says, and its best-of-N ranking result supports rendering several seeds and ranking them automatically.

title: GenAI Arena: An Open Evaluation Platform for Generative Models
finding: Crowdsourced pairwise-vote arena for 35 open image/video generative models (over 9000 votes in seven months); when MLLMs mimic human votes, the best (GPT-4o) reaches only 49.19 average accuracy and open MLLMs do worse.
why_for_us: Strong warning against using an off-the-shelf VLM as our video judge without validation; also a model for our human review: pairwise votes aggregated into a ranking with stated statistics.

title: MM-JudgeBias: A Benchmark for Evaluating Compositional Biases in MLLM-as-a-Judge
finding: Over 1,800 samples from 29 benchmarks with controlled perturbations of query, image and response diagnose nine bias types; experiments on 26 MLLMs reveal systematic modality neglect, asymmetric evaluation and instability under semantically irrelevant perturbations.
why_for_us: Before trusting a VLM judge on our clips, run a perturbation test (swap order, drop the image, paraphrase the prompt) and reject judges whose verdict changes.

title: VideoPhy: Evaluating Physical Commonsense for Video Generation
finding: Benchmark of physical commonsense in material interactions; human evaluation shows the best model, open CogVideoX-5B, follows both caption and physics in only 39.6% of instances; proposes the VideoCon-Physics auto-evaluator.
why_for_us: Calibrates expectations: open models fail physics most of the time, so shots with object interaction need explicit plausibility checks or human review, while static talking heads are lower risk.

title: GeneVA: A Dataset of Human Annotations for Generative Text to Video Artifacts
finding: 16,356 AI-generated videos with per-frame human artifact bounding boxes, labels, descriptions and quality ratings, plus a new spatio-temporal artifact taxonomy; an artifact detector and caption generator are trained on it.
why_for_us: Use its taxonomy as the label set for our blind review form (so reviewers tag why a clip fails) and consider its detector for localising mouth and hand artifacts.

title: Artifact-Bench: Evaluating MLLMs on Detecting and Assessing the Artifacts of AI-Generated Videos
finding: Three-level taxonomy of realism artifacts; on real-vs-AI classification, pairwise realism comparison and fine-grained artifact identification, 19 MLLMs show substantial limitations, many near or below random in hard settings, with significant misalignment to human perceptual preferences.
why_for_us: Further evidence that general VLMs are unreliable artifact judges; keep artifact detection in specialised metrics plus human review.

title: Temporal Stability Profiling of AI-Generated Short Videos: A Training-Free Metric Suite with Controlled-Perturbation Validation and a Case Study on Public Showcase Clips
finding: Training-free FFmpeg-only metric suite (activity, freeze ratio, flicker index, temporal jitter, shot-boundary count, duplicate-frame ratio); per author each metric moved in the expected direction for 15/15 perturbed clips (14/15 for hard cuts), and CRF 35 re-encoding changed metrics by at most 3.4% median.
why_for_us: Cheap CPU-side pre-gate that catches frozen segments, flicker and duplicated frames before any GPU scorer; single-author, uncited preprint, so validate on our clips first.

title: A Lip Sync Expert Is All You Need for Speech to Lip Generation In the Wild
finding: Wav2Lip trains against a pre-trained lip-sync discriminator and proposes new benchmarks and metrics to measure lip sync in unconstrained video; per authors its lip-sync accuracy is almost as good as real synced videos.
why_for_us: Reference protocol for the SyncNet-based LSE-D/LSE-C metrics we should compute instead of our rough audio-motion correlation.

title: A Deep Dive Into Neural Synchrony Evaluation for Audio-visual Translation
finding: Analyses agreement of SyncNet scores with human perception of lip synchrony, explains its predictions, and shows susceptibility to adversarial noise; notes SyncNet was not built for the many local asynchronies of dubbing-like settings.
why_for_us: Our Polish TTS-driven talking heads resemble dubbing; SyncNet scores alone may miss local desyncs, so pair them with windowed offsets and human spot-checks.

title: Audio-Visual Speech Representation Expert for Enhanced Talking Face Video Generation and Evaluation
finding: Uses AV-HuBERT as a lip-sync expert for training loss and introduces three new AV-HuBERT-based lip-sync evaluation metrics for a more comprehensive and robust assessment of synchronization.
why_for_us: AV-HuBERT-based sync metrics give a second, independent sync signal beside SyncNet LSE; check which of the two tracks our Polish reviewers better.

title: Software Lip-Sync Metrics Do Not Predict Delivered Audio-Visual Synchronisation: A Photodiode and Line-Output Measurement of Talking-Head Video Playback Against ITU-R BT.1359-1
finding: Photodiode plus line-output measurement over 24 system/player/resolution cells (3637 trials) found median delivered offsets of -210.9 to -79.2 ms with sound lagging everywhere; LSE-D and LSE-C were uncorrelated with delivered offset (r = -0.066 to +0.083).
why_for_us: Even a good file-level LSE does not guarantee sync on the viewer's player; check A/V timestamps and audio padding in our mux step and review clips in the target player.

title: ArcFace: Additive Angular Margin Loss for Deep Face Recognition
finding: Additive angular margin loss for discriminative face embeddings, plus sub-center ArcFace for robustness to label noise; the standard backbone behind identity-similarity metrics.
why_for_us: Add ArcFace cosine similarity between the reference portrait and sampled frames (min and mean over the clip) as an identity-drift gate for talking heads, replacing generic last-frame similarity for face shots.

title: Toward Verifiable and Reproducible Human Evaluation for Text-to-Image Generation
finding: Survey of 37 papers finds many rely only on automatic measures like FID or poorly described human evaluations; proposes a standardized protocol, shows in pilot data that automatic measures are incompatible with human perception, and gives design insights for reliable, conclusive human studies.
why_for_us: Template for writing down our blind-review protocol (instructions, scale, ratings per item, statistical test) so verdicts are reproducible across weeks and reviewers.

title: Rethinking FID: Towards a Better Evaluation Metric for Image Generation
finding: Shows FID contradicts human raters, misses gradual model improvement and distortion levels, and is inconsistent across sample sizes; proposes CMMD (CLIP embeddings with MMD) as an unbiased, sample-efficient alternative.
why_for_us: Do not add FID/FVD-style distribution metrics to a per-clip gate; at most use CMMD for comparing model versions over a batch of clips.

title: On the Content Bias in Fréchet Video Distance
finding: FVD rises only slightly under large temporal corruption and can be drastically lowered by selecting motionless videos without improving temporal quality, i.e. it is biased toward per-frame quality; features from large self-supervised video models reduce the bias.
why_for_us: Confirms FVD would reward frozen, static talking heads; never use it as a motion or temporal-quality signal in our gate.
